hints: State the two outer intervals where the product is positive.
walkthrough:
Set up the inequality and rearrange into standard quadratic form:
$$2x^2 - 6x + 5 > 13 \implies 2x^2 - 6x - 8 > 0 \implies x^2 - 3x - 4 > 0$$

Factorise the quadratic expression to identify the critical values:
$$(x - 4)(x + 1) > 0 \implies x = -1, \quad x = 4$$

Determine the outer intervals where the quadratic expression is strictly positive:
$$x < -1 \quad\text{or}\quad x > 4$$

ai_rubric.Quadratics and Inequalities: Sets up $2x^2 - 6x - 8 > 0$ and finds roots $x = -1, 4$ (M1A1). Obtains solution $x < -1$ or $x > 4$ (A1).

walkthrough:
Equate the line and curve equations to form a quadratic equation in $x$:
$$2x^2 - 6x + 5 = 2x + k \implies 2x^2 - 8x + (5 - k) = 0$$

Set the discriminant $b^2 - 4ac$ equal to zero for tangency (one point of intersection):
$$(-8)^2 - 4(2)(5 - k) = 0 \implies 64 - 8(5 - k) = 0$$

Solve the linear equation for $k$:
$$64 - 40 + 8k = 0 \implies 24 + 8k = 0 \implies 8k = -24 \implies k = -3$$

ai_rubric.Quadratics and Tangents: Equates equations to get $2x^2 - 8x + (5-k) = 0$ (M1). Applies discriminant $b^2 - 4ac = 0$ (DM1). Obtains $k = -3$ (A1).
